'''Chandler:''' {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Brock Adams]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Patty Murray]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Washington State}} The '''1992 United States Senate election in Washington''' was held on November 3, 1992. Incumbent Democratic Senator [[Brock Adams]] chose not to run for re-election to a second term after eight different women made allegations that he had engaged in various acts of sexual misconduct, including harassment and rape.{{Cite news|author1= Boardman, D. |author2=Gilmore, S. |author3=Nalder, E. |author4=Pryne, E.| title = 8 More Women Accuse Adams--Allegations of Two Decades of Sexual Harassment, Abuse - And a Rape| publisher =The Seattle Times| date =March 1, 1992| url =https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/19920301/1478550/8-more-women-accuse-adams| access-date =July 3, 2009}} Adams denied the allegations, but his popularity statewide was weakened considerably by them, and he chose to retire rather than risk costing the party his seat. State Senator [[Patty Murray]] defeated Republican [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Rod Chandler]] in the race to succeed Adams. Chandler seemed to have the upper hand in one of the debates until, for some unknown reason, he quoted the Roger Miller song "[[Dang Me]]."[http://www.seattlepi.com/connelly/285755_joel20.html Cantwell snubs McGavick on debates] By Joel Connelly ''[[Seattle Post-Intelligencer]]'' He was further damaged by the unpopularity of President [[George H. W.
